newsitem.title: JAPAN: China to ship up to 60,000 tonnes soybean to Japan.
newsitem.headline: China to ship up to 60,000 tonnes soybean to Japan.

text.p: China has agreed with Japanese trade houses to export up to 60,000 tonnes of soybeans to Japan for shipment between December 1996 and April 1997, Japanese and Chinese soybean traders said on Tuesday.

The Chinese grain trading agency agreed to deliver new-crop soybeans to the Japanese trade houses, at $380 a tonne for the December 1996 shipment and $395 for the January-April 1997 shipment, the traders said.

Officials from the Chinese grain agency Cereals, Oils and Feedstuffs Import and Export Corp and Heilongjiang province, which grows most of China's soybeans, were in Tokyo last week to hold negotiations with Japanese trade houses.
Chinese soybeans are mainly used for making miso, or bean paste, in Japan.
